Topics · One God, one message

Could the verse on rival groups be about me?

A verse that names no one speaks to every reader: a gentle mirror, Muslims first, with a door left open.

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا ۚ فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا ۚ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ٣٠ مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ٣١ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا۟ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوا۟ شِيَعًا ۖ كُلُّ حِزْبٍۭ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ٣٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fiṭrah[1145] of Allāh upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allāh.[1146] That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know. [Adhere to it], turning in repentance to Him, and fear Him and establish prayer and do not be of those who associate others with Allāh [Or] of those who have divided their religion and become sects, every faction rejoicing in what it has.[1147]

Translator's notes

[1145] The natural inborn inclination of man to worship his Creator prior to the corruption of his nature by external influences. Thus, Islāmic monotheism is described as the religion of fiṭrah - that of the inherent nature of mankind. [1146] i.e., let people remain true to their fiṭrah within the religion of Islām.

[1147] Of beliefs, opinions, customs, etc.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:30-32

Translation

Israel, return to Yahweh your God; for you have fallen because of your sin.

Original · Hebrew

שׁ֚וּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּ֥י כָשַׁ֖לְתָּ בַּעֲוֺנֶֽךָ׃

Hosea · 14:1

World English Bible

It is easy to read "each party rejoicing in what it holds" while thinking of others. The verses do not allow it. They open in address: set your face toward the religion, and do not be among those who split theirs. The command falls first on the one reading. The logic is plain. If rejoicing in what is ours exists in every party, my sense that my group is right feels just like the sense of those opposing it. That feeling alone cannot tell us apart.

A question for you

Who came to mind first?

If you sayAnother group
ThenMost people do that the first time. The verse describes that too, gently.
If you sayMy own group
ThenThat takes courage. A question remains: your group, or you?
If you sayI belong to no group
ThenEven without a group, each of us has views we are glad to hold. You might ask what you rejoice in holding.

Part 2 of 3

﴿لَّيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلَآ أَمَانِىِّ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ ۗ مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوٓءًا يُجْزَ بِهِۦ وَلَا يَجِدْ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا١٢٣ وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ مِن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ نَقِيرًا١٢٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

It [i.e., Paradise] is not [obtained] by your wishful thinking nor by that of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it, and he will not find besides Allāh a protector or a helper. And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:123-124

Translation

“I, Yahweh, search the mind. I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”

Original · Hebrew

אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה חֹקֵ֥ר לֵ֖ב בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת וְלָתֵ֤ת לְאִישׁ֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו כִּפְרִ֖י מַעֲלָלָֽיו׃

Jeremiah · 17:10

World English Bible

If the Quran were selling a group, it would excuse its own readers. This verse does the reverse: not by your wishes, nor by the wishes of the People of the Book. On a widely held reading, "your" means its own readers, and it comes first. So it is not a matter of what any group hopes for itself. The measure is set for every person: what they do. The next verse opens wide: male or female, doing good in faith, nothing lost. One rule for all, no reserved seats.

A question for you

Why might the verse begin with "your wishes" before mentioning anyone else?

If you saySo each begins with themselves
ThenThat changes how any sacred text is read: start with me before anyone else.
If you sayTo be fair
ThenThen fairness begins at home, which is harder than fairness to a stranger.
If you sayI am not sure
ThenThat is fine. Carry the question into the next part.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Translation

Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

Original · Hebrew

יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃

Isaiah · 55:7

World English Bible

The mirror is not complete without these two verses together. The first asks: do you tell people to do right and forget yourselves, while reading the Book? Anyone who reads the Book can stand near that forgetting. If the mirror stopped there it would be harsh. But the second comes from God, straight to those who have wronged themselves: do not despair. Whoever finds themselves in the first is invited in the second. The mirror is not there to make you sad. It is there so you can come back.

A question for you

What have you told others to do and forgotten in yourself?

The same in the other books
